overview: Island Tower is the newest Disney Vacation Club building at the Polynesian, a tower on the Seven Seas Lagoon with views toward Magic Kingdom.
suits: Families who want a modern villa with the Polynesian's location and amenities.
rooms: As a Disney Vacation Club resort, rooms range from studios with a kitchenette to multi-bedroom villas with a full kitchen and washer and dryer. You don't need to be a member to stay; you can book with cash like a regular hotel.
pools: Island Tower has its own pool, Cove Pool, with rows of lounge chairs and umbrellas in front of the tower and a splash area where a Moana figure rides a raft among the fountains. Guests can use the Polynesian's other pools too.
dining:
Island Tower has its own restaurant, Wailulu Bar & Grill, right on the lagoon at the foot of the tower. It's open-air under a big covered roof, with a bar, booths along the water and views across to Magic Kingdom and the Grand Floridian. Lunch and dinner are table service, and in the morning there's a grab-and-go breakfast of pastries and coffee. You don't need to stay at Island Tower to eat here.

Hours (from the sign at the restaurant, November 2026): breakfast 7 to 11 AM, restaurant 11 AM to 10 PM, bar 11 AM to 11 PM.

On the menu (prices as of fall 2026, before tax and tip):

  • Wayfinder Burger ($23): two pressed patties, American cheese, onion jam and a spicy volcano sauce on a sweet bun, with sweet potato fries or purple mac salad.
  • Poke Bowl ($26 with ahi tuna, $22 with teriyaki chicken or grilled tofu): sushi rice, pickled cucumbers, spicy poke sauce and macadamia nuts.
  • Ahi Tuna Crisps ($17): marinated ahi on fried wontons with avocado crema and sriracha aioli, good for sharing.
  • Teriyaki Chicken Sliders ($19) and Beef Short Rib Loco Moco ($33), with shiitake gravy, a crispy rice cake and a fried egg.
  • DOLE Whip Sundae ($8) for dessert, with hibiscus meringue and pineapple.
  • Tropical cocktails at the bar, plus a hibiscus iced tea if you're not drinking.

What's good:

  • Get the Wayfinder Burger. Reviewers rank it among the best burgers at Disney World. Swap the fries for the purple mac salad, which is the better side.
  • Share the Ahi Tuna Crisps to start, and get a poke bowl if you want something lighter. Even the tofu version gets raves.
  • The Loco Moco gets mixed reviews for $33, so the burger or a poke bowl is the safer pick.
  • Sit outside. The lagoon-side booths are the best seats, and the indoor room is plainer.
  • For Magic Kingdom fireworks, book about an hour before showtime and ask for a lagoon-side booth. A view isn't guaranteed, and you can't reserve a specific table. The Electrical Water Pageant floats past in the evening too.
  • You can book ahead like other Disney restaurants, and there's a walk-up waitlist at the podium or in the My Disney Experience app. Without a booking, expect a wait at dinner.
  • Not staying here? There's no parking at Island Tower. Polynesian parking is for guests with a dining reservation, so walk-ups should take the monorail from the Transportation and Ticket Center.

You can also use the Polynesian's other restaurants, including 'Ohana, Kona Cafe and Pineapple Lanai.
pros: Wailulu Bar & Grill on site, with fireworks views
cons: A walk to the Polynesian's monorail station
tips: Request a Magic Kingdom-facing room for fireworks views.
Use the boat to Magic Kingdom for a relaxing ride.
bestFor: Families who want a modern villa at the Polynesian.
